chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no deed except with an intention.
ai.seo_question: What is the role of intention in Islamic deeds?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this concise hadith from Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) serves as a cornerstone of Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the spiritual merit of an action is intrinsically tied to the sincerity of the heart. Scholars note that while the Arabic phrasing is brief, it encompasses both ritual worship (ibadat) and social transactions (mu'amalat), establishing intention as the essential criterion for distinguishing between mere habit and conscious devotion.
